title: Multiplicity of a root of a polynomial
statement:
Let $K$ be a field, $T$ an indeterminate and $K[T]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. For $P\in K[T]$ and $c\in K$, the multiplicity of $c$ as a root of $P$ is

$$
m_c(P)=\max\{m\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}:(T-c)^m\text{ divides }P\text{ in }K[T]\}\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}
$$

when $P\neq0$ (the set is finite because $\deg(T-c)^m=m\leq\deg P$ for every divisor $(T-c)^m$ of $P$), and $m_c(0)=0$. Thus $m_c(P)\geq1$ if and only if $P\neq0$ and $P(c)=0$, by the factor theorem; $c$ is a simple root of $P$ when $m_c(P)=1$.
